slug: 2026-03-31 Africa we have a data problem

facts.fact: Data Landscapers' 54-country review (an AI-assisted compilation, the author's analysis) states that rural primary schools in Cameroon predominantly use paper registers for administrative data, attendance and learning outcomes, that only 3% of public primary schools have computers, and scores Cameroon schools 1; the statement is undated, so the document's publication date is used.
facts.system: paper registers (no system named at school level)

systems.owner: aggregation at national level via INS
systems.tiers: central and regional levels; the document says implementation is delayed and it is not used at the point of service in rural schools
isolated pilot; one e-container in the Southwest

note: The paper fact names no system of class emis: it is the dated statement of absence the brief asks for, recorded under the sub-indicator's class. The document also says national policies (GESP, ETSS, ERSP) aim for an integrated EMIS, with no system described; 66.6% of administrative structures lack computers.
